note: Christian Religious Studies round 3 (part C): Acts, the Epistles and Christian living - love, fellowship, the Holy Spirit and mission, opposition, mission to the Gentiles, justification, law and grace, new life, joint heirs, humility, forgiveness, spiritual gifts, giving, civic responsibility, dignity of labour, second coming, impartiality, prayer, community living, corruption and sexual immorality - scripture-based and application items.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Love is patient and kind; love is not jealous or boastful; it is not arrogant or rude.' A church elder who constantly reminds members of how much he has done for the church is failing the test that love
questions.A: bears all things and endures all things
questions.B: is not boastful or arrogant
questions.C: does not rejoice at wrong
questions.D: is patient and kind
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:4: genuine love does not parade its achievements or seek recognition.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said that faith, hope and love abide, 'but the greatest of these is love', because
questions.A: faith and hope were given only to the apostles
questions.B: love is easier to practise than either faith or hope
questions.C: love never ends, whereas prophecy, tongues and knowledge will pass away
questions.D: love was the only gift the Corinthians possessed
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:8-13: love outlasts every gift and belongs to the perfect age to come.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: John wrote, 'If any one says, I love God, and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, cannot love God whom he has not seen.' A member who fasts weekly but refuses to greet a fellow member is
questions.A: keeping the first commandment while ignoring only a minor rule
questions.B: showing that love of God is more important than love of neighbour
questions.C: practising the higher form of love that John commended
questions.D: contradicting his claim to love God by his hatred of his brother
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:20-21: love for God is proved by love for the brethren; the two cannot be separated.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.' Jesus demonstrated this
questions.A: by washing the feet of the disciples at the supper
questions.B: by dying on the cross for those he called his friends
questions.C: by feeding the five thousand in the wilderness
questions.D: by raising Lazarus from the dead at Bethany
questions.explanation: John 15:13; Romans 5:8: 'While we were yet sinners Christ died for us.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When a lawyer asked, 'Who is my neighbour?' Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan and then asked, 'Which of these three proved neighbour to the man who fell among the robbers?' Jesus turned the question round to show that
questions.A: priests and Levites were excused from helping the wounded because of the rules about ritual purity
questions.B: Samaritans were better neighbours than Jews by nature and should be preferred as travelling companions
questions.C: the real issue is not who deserves my love but whether I act as a neighbour to anyone in need
questions.D: only those who live in the same town or village can properly be regarded as one's neighbours
questions.explanation: Luke 10:29-37: 'Go and do likewise' - neighbour-love is defined by the one who shows mercy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: John wrote, 'In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the expiation for our sins.' This teaches that
questions.A: only those who first love God are loved by him
questions.B: human love for God earns the sending of the Son
questions.C: love is a feeling that cannot be commanded
questions.D: God's love came first and is the source and model of our love
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:10, 19: 'We love, because he first loved us.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Pentecost the believers 'devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers'. A church that concentrates on entertainment and fund-raising while neglecting Bible teaching and prayer has departed from
questions.A: the instructions Paul gave to the church at Corinth
questions.B: the pattern of the first Christian community in Jerusalem
questions.C: the decision of the Council of Jerusalem
questions.D: the practice of the synagogue in Nazareth
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42: teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer were the four marks of the early church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Barnabas sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet. His act was praised because
questions.A: the apostles had demanded that every member sell his land
questions.B: he was the richest member of the Jerusalem church
questions.C: it was a voluntary gift for the needs of the whole community
questions.D: he kept part of the price for his own use
questions.explanation: Acts 4:36-37: Barnabas, 'son of encouragement', gave freely, in contrast to Ananias and Sapphira.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter told Ananias, 'While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal?' This shows that the sin of Ananias and Sapphira was
questions.A: giving too small a portion of the price to the apostles
questions.B: selling property that belonged to the church
questions.C: refusing to sell their property like the others
questions.D: lying to the Holy Spirit by pretending to give the whole price
questions.explanation: Acts 5:3-4: they were free to keep the money; their sin was deceit that sought credit for generosity they had not shown.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The Hellenists murmured against the Hebrews because their widows were neglected in the daily distribution. The apostles solved the problem by
questions.A: expelling the Hellenists from the church in Jerusalem and sending them to form a church in Samaria
questions.B: appointing seven men of good repute to serve tables while they gave themselves to prayer and the word
questions.C: sending the Hebrew widows back to their home towns so that the Hellenist widows could be fed first
questions.D: abolishing the daily distribution altogether and telling every family to provide for its own widows
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1-6: Stephen, Philip and five others were chosen, and the word of God increased.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church treasurer publicly announces a huge pledge, is applauded, and later secretly pays only a fraction while insisting he paid everything. His conduct resembles that of
questions.A: Simon the sorcerer
questions.B: Barnabas of Cyprus
questions.C: Ananias and Sapphira
questions.D: Cornelius the centurion
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1-11: the couple lied about the amount given in order to appear more generous than they were.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Luke records that the early believers 'were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things which he possessed was his own'. A youth fellowship whose members pay each other's school fees and share food in hard times is practising
questions.A: the Nazirite vow of separation
questions.B: the tithing law of the Old Testament
questions.C: the collection Paul organised for Jerusalem
questions.D: the communal sharing of the early church
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32-35: 'there was not a needy person among them' because the believers shared what they had.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: On the day of Pentecost the crowd asked, 'What does this mean?' while others mocked, saying, 'They are filled with new wine.' Peter answered that
questions.A: the disciples had indeed been drinking at the feast, but only to celebrate the resurrection
questions.B: this was the fulfilment of Joel's prophecy that God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh
questions.C: the crowd should return to their countries at once and wait for the apostles to visit them
questions.D: only the twelve apostles could ever receive the Holy Spirit, so the crowd need not be concerned
questions.explanation: Acts 2:14-21: Peter quoted Joel 2:28-32 and preached Christ crucified and risen.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: When the crowd at Pentecost were 'cut to the heart' and asked, 'Brethren, what shall we do?' Peter told them to
questions.A: wait in Jerusalem until the Spirit came upon them
questions.B: go back to the temple and offer a sin offering
questions.C: repent and be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins
questions.D: sell their possessions and give the money to the apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 2:37-41: about three thousand were baptised and added that day.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: Jesus promised, 'The Counsellor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.' This promise assured the disciples that
questions.A: the Spirit would replace the need for prayer
questions.B: they would never need to study the scriptures again
questions.C: Jesus would remain physically present with them for ever
questions.D: the Spirit would guide them into the truth after Jesus had gone
questions.explanation: John 14:26 and 16:13: the Spirit continues the teaching ministry of Jesus in the church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: The Holy Spirit said to the church at Antioch, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.' This shows that
questions.A: the apostles in Jerusalem appointed all missionaries
questions.B: the Spirit directs the missionary work of the church
questions.C: Antioch had replaced Jerusalem as the mother church
questions.D: Barnabas and Saul chose their own field of work
questions.explanation: Acts 13:1-3: the church fasted, prayed, laid hands on them and sent them off, 'being sent out by the Holy Spirit'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: Philip was directed by the Spirit to join the chariot of the Ethiopian eunuch, who was reading Isaiah 53. Philip
questions.A: refused to speak to him because he was a foreigner
questions.B: told him to go to Jerusalem and ask the apostles for an explanation
questions.C: began with that scripture and told him the good news of Jesus, and baptised him
questions.D: sold him a copy of the gospel of Matthew
questions.explanation: Acts 8:26-39: the Spirit led Philip to a Gentile seeker, and the gospel began to reach Africa.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: A church committee chooses a mission field purely because it is comfortable and well funded, without prayer. Acts 13 and 16 suggest they have forgotten that
questions.A: mission work should be confined to one's own tribe and language until every member is converted
questions.B: missionaries should always go first to the wealthiest cities, where the greatest support is found
questions.C: only ordained apostles from Jerusalem may choose a mission field for the churches to support
questions.D: the Spirit calls and directs missionaries, sometimes forbidding one route and opening another
questions.explanation: Acts 16:6-10: Paul was forbidden by the Spirit to preach in Asia and was directed by a vision to Macedonia.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After being beaten by order of the Sanhedrin, the apostles left 'rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonour for the name'. Their attitude shows that
questions.A: the beating had been light and did them no real harm
questions.B: suffering for Christ was regarded as an honour, not a cause for despair
questions.C: they expected the council to apologise the next day
questions.D: they had decided to stop preaching in the temple
questions.explanation: Acts 5:40-42: they continued every day in the temple and at home to teach and preach Jesus as the Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Stephen's speech before the council ended with the charge, 'You stiff-necked people... you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you.' The council responded by
questions.A: referring the case to the Roman governor Felix
questions.B: releasing him because his speech had convinced them
questions.C: grinding their teeth, casting him out of the city and stoning him
questions.D: appointing him to preach in the synagogue of the Freedmen
questions.explanation: Acts 7:51-60: Stephen saw the Son of man standing at God's right hand and died praying for his killers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Stephen's death a great persecution scattered the church, 'and those who were scattered went about preaching the word'. The result was that
questions.A: the believers renounced their faith to save their lives
questions.B: the church in Jerusalem ceased to exist for many years
questions.C: the apostles fled to Rome and never returned
questions.D: the persecution spread the gospel to Samaria and beyond instead of stopping it
questions.explanation: Acts 8:1-4: opposition became the means of expansion, fulfilling Acts 1:8.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword and imprisoned Peter, but 'earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church'. The outcome was that
questions.A: Peter was executed the following morning
questions.B: an angel released Peter from prison during the night
questions.C: Herod repented and became a Christian
questions.D: the church paid a ransom for Peter's release
questions.explanation: Acts 12:1-17: Peter's chains fell off and he walked out past the guards to the house where the church was praying.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Philippi, after being beaten and thrown into the inner prison with their feet in the stocks, Paul and Silas
questions.A: bribed the jailer to let them escape before dawn
questions.B: cursed the magistrates and demanded to see the emperor
questions.C: prayed and sang hymns to God at midnight while the prisoners listened
questions.D: renounced their Roman citizenship to gain release
questions.explanation: Acts 16:22-34: an earthquake opened the doors, and the jailer and his household believed and were baptised.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A Christian teacher is mocked by colleagues for refusing to falsify results, yet she continues cheerfully and wins some of them over. Her response reflects the apostles' example of
questions.A: reporting the mockers to the authorities for punishment
questions.B: withdrawing from public life until persecution ceases
questions.C: returning insult for insult to defend the gospel
questions.D: rejoicing under dishonour for the name of Christ and continuing to witness
questions.explanation: Acts 5:41-42; 1 Peter 4:14, 16: 'If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Peter came to Cornelius he said, 'You yourselves know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with or to visit any one of another nation; but God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.' Peter learned this lesson through
questions.A: the teaching of Gamaliel in Jerusalem
questions.B: the vision of the great sheet let down from heaven
questions.C: a letter from Paul about the Gentile churches
questions.D: the conversion of the Ethiopian eunuch by Philip
questions.explanation: Acts 10:9-16, 28: the vision of clean and unclean animals prepared Peter to accept Gentiles.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: While Peter was still speaking at the house of Cornelius, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word. Peter then said,
questions.A: 'Your money perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money.'
questions.B: 'Silver and gold have I none, but what I have I give you.'
questions.C: 'Can any one forbid water for baptising these people who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?'
questions.D: 'We must obey God rather than men.'
questions.explanation: Acts 10:44-48: God's gift of the Spirit to Gentiles settled the question of their admission.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Some men from Judea taught the brethren at Antioch, 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.' The Council of Jerusalem replied that Gentile believers should
questions.A: return to their former religions until the apostles could visit them, since the question could not be settled by letter
questions.B: be circumcised and keep the whole law of Moses before baptism, exactly as the men from Judea had taught them at Antioch
questions.C: form a separate church with its own elders and never eat with Jewish believers, so that neither group would be offended
questions.D: abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled and from unchastity, but need not be circumcised
questions.explanation: Acts 15:1-29: James' judgment was that they 'should not trouble those of the Gentiles who turn to God'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the Council of Jerusalem Peter argued, 'God made no distinction between us and them, but cleansed their hearts by faith. Now therefore why do you make trial of God by putting a yoke upon the neck of the disciples?' The 'yoke' referred to
questions.A: the Roman taxes imposed on the churches of Asia
questions.B: the demand that Gentiles keep the law of Moses in order to be saved
questions.C: the persecution of the church by King Herod
questions.D: the requirement that Gentiles pay for the temple sacrifices
questions.explanation: Acts 15:7-11: salvation is 'through the grace of the Lord Jesus' for Jew and Gentile alike.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Pisidian Antioch, when the Jews contradicted Paul and reviled him, Paul and Barnabas said, 'Since you thrust it from you... behold, we turn to the Gentiles.' They justified this by quoting the prophecy,
questions.A: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this was the Lord's doing.'
questions.B: 'Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel, which means God with us.'
questions.C: 'I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.'
questions.D: 'Out of Egypt have I called my son, and I will gather the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth.'
questions.explanation: Acts 13:44-48: the Gentiles rejoiced, and 'as many as were ordained to eternal life believed'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A congregation insists that converts from another ethnic group must adopt its language and dress before they can be baptised. This resembles the error corrected at
questions.A: the shipwreck of Paul at Malta
questions.B: the stoning of Stephen
questions.C: the conversion of Saul on the Damascus road
questions.D: the Council of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 15: the church decided not to burden Gentile converts with Jewish customs as a condition of salvation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote that in Christ 'there is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus'. This teaches that
questions.A: Jews and Greeks should worship in separate buildings
questions.B: the gospel abolishes barriers of race, class and sex within the people of God
questions.C: slavery was abolished throughout the Roman empire by Paul
questions.D: there are no differences of role or gift among Christians
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:28: all who are baptised into Christ share equally in the promise to Abraham.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'For by grace you have been saved through faith; and this is not your own doing, it is the gift of God - not because of works, lest any man should boast.' A church member who says, 'God must accept me because of my thirty years of service,' has misunderstood
questions.A: that faith is unnecessary once a person has served the church
questions.B: that good works are forbidden to those who are saved by grace
questions.C: that salvation is God's free gift received by faith, not a wage earned by works
questions.D: that long service in the church is the only true evidence of faith
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:8-9: boasting is excluded because justification rests on grace alone.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul argued that Abraham was reckoned righteous before he was circumcised, in order to show that
questions.A: Abraham earned his righteousness by obeying the law
questions.B: circumcision was abolished in the days of Abraham
questions.C: only the descendants of Abraham can be justified
questions.D: Abraham is the father of all who believe, whether circumcised or not
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9-12: faith, not the sign of circumcision, was the ground of Abraham's righteousness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Now to one who works, his wages are not reckoned as a gift but as his due. And to one who does not work but trusts him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness.' Paul contrasts
questions.A: the wages of a labourer and the salary of a civil servant
questions.B: earning acceptance with God by works and receiving it freely by faith
questions.C: the ungodly who work hard and the godly who are lazy
questions.D: faith in Abraham and faith in Moses
questions.explanation: Romans 4:4-5: justification is a gift to those who trust God, not a payment for merit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said to the Galatians, 'If justification were through the law, then Christ died to no purpose.' He meant that
questions.A: the Galatians should combine faith in Christ with circumcision to be safe
questions.B: Christ died only for those who had already kept the law perfectly
questions.C: seeking righteousness through law-keeping makes the death of Christ unnecessary and empties it of meaning
questions.D: the law was abolished so that Christians may live as they please
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:21: to add works of law to faith is to deny the sufficiency of the cross.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.' A believer who is constantly terrified that God will reject her over every small failing needs to understand that
questions.A: God's acceptance is withdrawn each time a believer sins and must be regained by fresh repentance
questions.B: peace with God is reserved for those who never fail, so her fear is the proper response to sin
questions.C: she should increase her good works until the fear disappears and God is satisfied with her record
questions.D: justification gives a settled peace with God based on Christ's work, not on her performance
questions.explanation: Romans 5:1-2: the justified stand in grace and rejoice in hope, not in fear.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James wrote, 'Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.' Paul wrote that a man is justified by faith apart from works of law. The two teachings agree because
questions.A: James rejected Paul's gospel and taught salvation by works, but the church later decided that both were right
questions.B: Paul speaks of how a person is accepted by God, while James speaks of the works that prove faith is genuine
questions.C: Paul later changed his mind and accepted James' position that works must be added to faith for salvation
questions.D: the two apostles were writing about two different covenants, one for Jews and the other for Gentiles
questions.explanation: James 2:14-26 attacks a dead, merely verbal faith; Paul attacks reliance on works for acceptance - both agree that true faith works through love (Galatians 5:6).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Through the law comes knowledge of sin,' and, 'I should not have known what it is to covet if the law had not said, You shall not covet.' This shows that a function of the law is to
questions.A: make coveting acceptable in certain circumstances
questions.B: remove sin from the hearts of those who study it
questions.C: expose sin and make people aware of their guilt
questions.D: replace the need for a Saviour
questions.explanation: Romans 3:20 and 7:7: the law reveals sin but cannot cure it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul asked, 'Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?' He was answering the objection that
questions.A: grace is available only to those who never sin
questions.B: the law of Moses had been too strict for Gentiles
questions.C: Christians must be circumcised to receive grace
questions.D: free grace encourages people to sin without restraint
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1-4: those united with Christ in baptism have died to sin and are to walk in newness of life.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A young convert says, 'Since I am under grace, it does not matter how I live.' Paul's answer would be that
questions.A: he is correct, since the law has no more relevance for a Christian's conduct once he has been baptised into Christ
questions.B: grace frees believers from sin's dominion so that they become slaves of righteousness, not so that they may sin freely
questions.C: he should return to keeping the whole law of Moses to be safe, since grace alone cannot restrain the flesh
questions.D: grace is withdrawn from anyone who asks such a question, and he must be baptised again before he can be restored
questions.explanation: Romans 6:14-18: 'You who were once slaves of sin have become... slaves of righteousness.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote to the Galatians, 'For freedom Christ has set us free; stand fast therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.' The 'yoke of slavery' he warned against was
questions.A: the payment of the temple tax by Gentile believers
questions.B: the Roman system of slavery in the province of Galatia
questions.C: the attempt to secure salvation by circumcision and law-keeping
questions.D: obedience to the moral teaching of Jesus
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:1-4: 'You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul described the law as 'holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good', yet insisted that it could not give life. The law's weakness lay in
questions.A: its abolition by the Roman authorities
questions.B: the fact that Moses wrote it down inaccurately
questions.C: its being given only to the tribe of Levi
questions.D: human sinful nature, which the law could expose but not change
questions.explanation: Romans 7:12 and 8:3: 'God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do: sending his own Son.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said Christ is 'the end of the law, that every one who has faith may be justified'. Christians therefore relate to the law as
questions.A: a set of rules that must be kept perfectly before God will accept them
questions.B: a standard fulfilled in Christ and written on the heart by the Spirit, not as a way of earning salvation
questions.C: an ancient document with no bearing on how believers live
questions.D: a burden imposed only on Jewish Christians
questions.explanation: Romans 10:4 and 8:4: the just requirement of the law is fulfilled in those who walk according to the Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul urged the Ephesians to 'put off your old nature which belongs to your former manner of life... and put on the new nature, created after the likeness of God'. He then gave practical examples, including
questions.A: 'If any one will not work, let him not eat, for we hear that some of you are living in idleness.'
questions.B: 'Let every person be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God.'
questions.C: 'Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labour, doing honest work with his hands.'
questions.D: 'Owe no one anything, except to love each other, for he who loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law.'
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:22-32: putting off the old nature includes truthfulness, honest work, wholesome speech and forgiveness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul listed the works of the flesh as including 'immorality, impurity, licentiousness, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, anger, selfishness, dissension, party spirit, envy, drunkenness'. A believer who claims to be Spirit-filled but constantly stirs up quarrels and factions in church is showing
questions.A: the boldness of the apostles before the council
questions.B: the fruit of the Spirit called faithfulness
questions.C: the gift of discernment of spirits
questions.D: works of the flesh rather than the fruit of the Spirit
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:19-23: strife, dissension and party spirit belong to the flesh; the Spirit produces peace and gentleness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me.' This describes
questions.A: Paul's physical death on a cross in Rome
questions.B: a new identity in which the believer's life is governed by Christ
questions.C: the loss of individual personality in the church
questions.D: a ritual performed by the Galatians at baptism
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:20: 'the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A former armed robber who now runs a legitimate business and returns to visit prisoners with the gospel illustrates Paul's teaching that
questions.A: believers should avoid all contact with criminals
questions.B: the works of the flesh cannot be overcome in this life
questions.C: in Christ the old has passed away and the new has come
questions.D: salvation is earned by making up for past sins
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17: 'If any one is in Christ, he is a new creation.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Colossians, 'Put to death therefore what is earthly in you: immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.' Covetousness is called idolatry because
questions.A: coveting was punished by the same penalty as idolatry under Roman law
questions.B: the Colossians made statues of gold and worshipped them
questions.C: only pagans were tempted to be covetous
questions.D: the greedy person makes possessions the object of his trust and devotion in place of God
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:5; compare Matthew 6:24: 'You cannot serve God and mammon.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Do not be conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewal of your mind.' A student who joins in examination malpractice because 'everybody does it' is
questions.A: proving that his mind has been renewed by the Spirit
questions.B: being conformed to the world instead of being transformed
questions.C: presenting his body as a living sacrifice
questions.D: discerning the will of God, which is good and acceptable
questions.explanation: Romans 12:1-2: the renewed mind resists the pressure of the surrounding culture.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'You did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the spirit of sonship. When we cry, Abba! Father! it is the Spirit himself bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God.' This shows that
questions.A: only the apostles were permitted to call God 'Father'
questions.B: Christians must remain fearful in order to be accepted by God
questions.C: the believer's assurance of sonship comes from the inner witness of the Spirit
questions.D: sonship is proved by the size of one's inheritance on earth
questions.explanation: Romans 8:15-16: Abba is an intimate Aramaic word for Father, used by Jesus himself.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: Paul said believers are 'heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him'. A prosperity preacher who teaches that true Christians never suffer contradicts
questions.A: the doctrine that Christ was raised from the dead
questions.B: the teaching that Christians are children of God
questions.C: the promise that the Spirit bears witness with our spirit
questions.D: the link Paul makes between sharing Christ's sufferings and sharing His glory
questions.explanation: Romans 8:17: suffering with Christ is part of the path to glory, not a sign of God's rejection.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: Paul wrote that 'the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us'. He meant that
questions.A: Christians do not really suffer in this life
questions.B: the future inheritance far outweighs present hardship
questions.C: glory is given now to those who suffer most
questions.D: suffering is always caused by the believer's own sin
questions.explanation: Romans 8:18: the hope of glory puts present troubles in proportion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: In Galatians Paul said that 'when the time had fully come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons'. Adoption means that believers
questions.A: are related to God only by the law of Moses
questions.B: must serve as slaves in the household of God
questions.C: are made full members of God's family with the rights of heirs
questions.D: become sons of Abraham by circumcision
questions.explanation: Galatians 4:4-7: 'So through God you are no longer a slave but a son, and if a son then an heir.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: Peter described the believer's inheritance as 'imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you'. This contrasts with earthly inheritances, which
questions.A: are more valuable than anything kept in heaven
questions.B: are always shared equally among children
questions.C: are received only after the death of the father
questions.D: can be lost, spoilt or squandered
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:3-5: the heavenly inheritance is secure because God guards both it and those who will receive it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Philippians, 'Do nothing from selfishness or conceit, but in humility count others better than yourselves. Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.' A prefect who takes credit for his classmates' work is failing to
questions.A: have the mind of Christ, who was obedient unto death
questions.B: count others better than himself
questions.C: work out his salvation with fear and trembling
questions.D: shine as a light in a crooked generation
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3-4: humility puts the interests and honour of others before one's own.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote that Christ 'humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name which is above every name.' This teaches that
questions.A: humility always brings promotion in this life
questions.B: Christ was exalted because he demanded recognition
questions.C: the way to true exaltation is through humble obedience
questions.D: Christ was not divine until after the resurrection
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:8-11: 'Whoever humbles himself will be exalted' (Luke 14:11) is supremely illustrated in Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter wrote, 'Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.' The image of clothing suggests that humility
questions.A: is needed only by young people towards their elders
questions.B: can be put on only on special religious occasions
questions.C: is a garment worn by priests in the temple
questions.D: should be visible in a believer's conduct at all times
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 5:5-6: 'Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that in due time he may exalt you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The disciples argued about who was the greatest. Jesus set a child in their midst and said, 'Whoever humbles himself like this child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.' He meant that greatness in the kingdom belongs to
questions.A: those who are physically small like children
questions.B: those who are humble and dependent, not to those who seek status
questions.C: the youngest member of every congregation
questions.D: those who have the most children
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:1-4: a child had no status in that society; Jesus made humility the measure of greatness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A choir leader who insists on sitting on the front row at every service so that visitors will notice him is behaving like the guests Jesus described who
questions.A: refused to wear a wedding garment
questions.B: made excuses and would not come to the banquet
questions.C: chose the places of honour at a marriage feast
questions.D: came in from the streets and lanes of the city
questions.explanation: Luke 14:7-11: 'When you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place... every one who exalts himself will be humbled.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the unforgiving servant, the king said, 'You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you besought me; and should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?' The parable teaches that
questions.A: small debts matter more to God than large ones
questions.B: debts should never be forgiven under any circumstances
questions.C: kings are more merciful than ordinary servants
questions.D: those who have received God's forgiveness must forgive others
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:23-35: the servant forgiven ten thousand talents refused to forgive a hundred denarii.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church member who was forgiven a large loan by a fellow member later has her tenant arrested over a small unpaid rent. She resembles
questions.A: the prodigal son's father
questions.B: the unforgiving servant in Jesus' parable
questions.C: the good Samaritan
questions.D: Joseph forgiving his brothers
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:28-30: having received mercy, the servant seized his fellow servant by the throat over a trifling debt.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Joseph told his brothers, 'Fear not, for am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.' Joseph was able to forgive because he
questions.A: was too powerful for the brothers to harm him again
questions.B: had forgotten how his brothers had treated him
questions.C: saw God's purpose at work even in the wrong done to him
questions.D: wanted the brothers to remain his slaves in Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 50:19-21: Joseph refused revenge and provided for his brothers and their children.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Colossians, 'As the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.' The measure of Christian forgiveness is therefore
questions.A: the custom of one's community or family
questions.B: the number of times the offender says sorry
questions.C: the seriousness of the offence committed
questions.D: the forgiveness that Christ has extended to the believer
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:13 and Ephesians 4:32: believers forgive as freely as they have been forgiven in Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the prodigal son, the elder brother was angry and refused to go in to the feast. His attitude represents
questions.A: the joy of heaven over one sinner who repents
questions.B: those who resent God's free forgiveness of repentant sinners
questions.C: the humility of the tax collector in the temple
questions.D: the patience of the father who waited for his son
questions.explanation: Luke 15:25-32: the elder brother mirrors the Pharisees who grumbled that Jesus received sinners.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus taught, 'If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him; and if he sins against you seven times in the day, and turns to you seven times, and says, I repent, you must forgive him.' This teaches that forgiveness should be
questions.A: withheld until the offender has paid compensation
questions.B: granted only once to each person in a lifetime
questions.C: unlimited and repeated whenever the offender repents
questions.D: offered only to members of one's own family
questions.explanation: Luke 17:3-4; compare Matthew 18:22: 'seventy times seven'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit... To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.' Spiritual gifts are therefore given
questions.A: so that gifted members may be honoured above the rest
questions.B: only to pastors and evangelists who lead congregations
questions.C: as rewards for those who have been Christians the longest
questions.D: for the benefit of the whole church, not for personal display
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:4-7: every gift serves the common good of the body.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said, 'If the foot should say, Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body, that would not make it any less a part of the body.' He was addressing members who
questions.A: wanted to leave the church and start their own fellowship
questions.B: felt inferior because they lacked the more spectacular gifts
questions.C: were proud of their gifts and despised others
questions.D: believed that the body of Christ had only one member
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:14-20: every member is needed, however humble its function.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church usher feels useless because she cannot preach or sing. Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians 12 reminds her that
questions.A: she should stop ushering until she receives a better gift, since ushering is not listed among the gifts
questions.B: only those who can preach or prophesy have received a spiritual gift, and the rest serve without one
questions.C: God has arranged every member in the body as He chose, and the less visible parts are indispensable
questions.D: the eye is the only member that matters in the body, and the other parts exist merely to support it
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:18-22: 'the parts of the body which seem to be weaker are indispensable'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul preferred prophecy to uninterpreted tongues in the assembly because
questions.A: the Corinthians did not possess the gift of tongues and were only pretending to speak in them
questions.B: tongues were a gift given only to the twelve apostles and had ceased before Paul's time
questions.C: prophecy was easier to fake than speaking in tongues and therefore easier to control
questions.D: prophecy edifies the church, whereas tongues without interpretation edify only the speaker
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:1-5, 19: 'In church I would rather speak five words with my mind... than ten thousand words in a tongue.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul concluded his instructions on the use of gifts in worship with the words, 'All things should be done decently and in order,' because
questions.A: the Roman authorities forbade noisy meetings
questions.B: God is not a God of confusion but of peace
questions.C: only the elders were allowed to speak in the assembly
questions.D: spiritual gifts had ceased in the church at Corinth
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:33, 40: orderly worship reflects the character of God and builds up the church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A member who speaks in tongues loudly during the sermon so that no one can hear the preacher is disregarding Paul's instruction that
questions.A: the preacher should stop and wait for the tongue to finish
questions.B: tongues are the greatest of all the gifts and must never be restrained
questions.C: if there is no interpreter, the speaker should keep silence in church and speak to himself and to God
questions.D: only women should speak in tongues in the assembly
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:27-28: tongues in public worship require interpretation and order.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Each one must do as he has made up his mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.' A pastor who locks the church doors until a target sum has been collected is violating the principle that
questions.A: the rich should give more than the poor
questions.B: only tithes and not offerings are acceptable to God
questions.C: giving should be done in secret without any record
questions.D: giving should be voluntary and cheerful, not forced
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7: compulsion destroys the cheerfulness that God loves.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said, 'He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.' He was encouraging the Corinthians to
questions.A: plant more crops in order to become wealthy
questions.B: give generously to the collection for the poor saints in Jerusalem
questions.C: give only when they were certain of a financial return
questions.D: sell their farms and give the money to the apostles
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:1-8: the context is the relief fund for Jerusalem, and generosity is met by God's sufficiency.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul commended the Macedonians because 'their abundance of joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of liberality... they gave according to their means, and beyond their means, of their own free will'. This teaches that
questions.A: poverty is a sign of God's blessing on a church
questions.B: only the poor are expected to give to the church
questions.C: generous giving depends on willingness, not on wealth
questions.D: Christians should give until they become destitute
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 8:1-5: 'first they gave themselves to the Lord and to us by the will of God'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul motivated the Corinthians to give by reminding them of 'the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich'. The supreme model for Christian giving is therefore
questions.A: the offering of the Pharisee in the temple
questions.B: the tithe that Abraham gave to Melchizedek
questions.C: the generosity of the rich young ruler
questions.D: the self-giving of Christ in his incarnation and death
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 8:9: giving is a response to grace received.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul instructed that the collection be set aside 'on the first day of every week' by each person 'as he may prosper', so that
questions.A: the apostles could take the money for their own use
questions.B: giving would be regular, planned and proportionate to income
questions.C: only the wealthy would be required to contribute
questions.D: the church would not need to give again for many years
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 16:1-2: systematic, proportionate giving rather than emotional, occasional appeals.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God.' He gave as the reason that the ruler
questions.A: has power to forgive sins in the name of God and to admit people to the church
questions.B: is always righteous and can never make an unjust law, since God appointed him
questions.C: is God's servant for your good and an avenger who executes wrath on the wrongdoer
questions.D: will reward Christians with positions in government if they support him faithfully
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-4: government exists by God's ordinance to restrain evil and promote good.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul urged 'that supplications, prayers, intercessions and thanksgivings be made for all men, for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life'. A church that curses its national leaders every Sunday is neglecting
questions.A: the duty to evangelise government officials
questions.B: the duty to pay taxes to whom taxes are due
questions.C: the duty to obey God rather than men
questions.D: the duty to pray for those in authority
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 2:1-2: prayer for rulers, even pagan ones, is a Christian obligation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter and John told the Sanhedrin, 'Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge.' Together with Romans 13, this teaches that Christian obedience to the state
questions.A: is absolute, whatever the authorities command, since all authority comes from God
questions.B: is real but limited: when the state commands what God forbids, God must be obeyed
questions.C: applies only to Christian governments and may be withheld from pagan rulers
questions.D: can be withdrawn whenever taxes are raised or the church's property is threatened
questions.explanation: Acts 4:19-20 and 5:29: 'We must obey God rather than men' - the exception that limits Romans 13.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A Christian civil servant is ordered by his director to destroy evidence of fraud. He refuses but continues to perform all his lawful duties diligently. He is correctly applying
questions.A: the teaching that civil servants are exempt from Romans 13 because they are part of the state
questions.B: the teaching that all human authority must be resisted because it is opposed to God
questions.C: obedience to lawful authority combined with the principle of obeying God rather than men
questions.D: the principle that the end justifies the means, since exposing fraud is a good end
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-7 with Acts 5:29: submission to authority stops where sin begins, without rebellion in other matters.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter wrote, 'Be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution... Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the emperor.' This was written when the emperor was
questions.A: Peter's own relative from Galilee, which explains why the apostle urged such loyalty
questions.B: a Christian who had built churches throughout the empire and protected the apostles
questions.C: a Jew who had restored the temple in Jerusalem and invited Peter to preach there
questions.D: a pagan ruler, showing that respect for authority does not depend on the ruler's faith
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:13-17: written under Nero or a similar pagan emperor; honour is due to the office.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Pay all of them their dues, taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due.' A trader who under-declares her income to avoid tax is
questions.A: acting rightly if the government is corrupt
questions.B: failing in a duty Paul lays on Christians towards the state
questions.C: obeying God rather than men
questions.D: exercising the freedom Christ purchased for her
questions.explanation: Romans 13:6-7: paying taxes honestly is part of Christian submission to the authorities God has ordained.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul reminded the Thessalonians, 'We were not idle when we were with you, we did not eat any one's bread without paying, but with toil and labour we worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you.' Paul worked in order to
questions.A: avoid preaching the gospel in public
questions.B: become wealthy from the tent-making trade
questions.C: give the believers an example to imitate
questions.D: prove that apostles were not entitled to support
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 3:7-9: 'not because we have not that right, but to give you in our conduct an example to imitate'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul instructed, 'Whatever your task, work heartily, as serving the Lord and not men.' A cleaner who does her job thoroughly even when the supervisor is absent is
questions.A: seeking the praise of men rather than of God
questions.B: working only for the wages she receives
questions.C: wasting effort that could be used for church activities
questions.D: serving the Lord in her ordinary work, as Paul taught
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:23-24: all honest work done for the Lord has dignity and will be rewarded by Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul commanded, 'Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labour, doing honest work with his hands, so that he may be able to give to those in need.' Honest work is presented as
questions.A: a punishment reserved for converted thieves
questions.B: the means of meeting one's own needs and helping others
questions.C: less spiritual than full-time preaching
questions.D: unnecessary for those who have faith
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:28: work replaces stealing and makes generosity possible.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Genesis records that God 'took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it' before the fall. This shows that work is
questions.A: meant only for those who cannot afford servants
questions.B: a punishment introduced only after Adam sinned
questions.C: part of God's original good purpose for man, not merely a curse
questions.D: less honourable than rest and worship
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:15: labour belonged to paradise; the toil and thorns of Genesis 3:17-19 came after the fall.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote that some at Thessalonica were 'living in idleness, mere busybodies, not doing any work'. He commanded such persons 'to do their work in quietness and to earn their own living'. A graduate who refuses every job that is 'below his level' while depending on his relatives is
questions.A: practising the communal sharing of the early church
questions.B: rightly waiting for the work God has prepared for him
questions.C: following the example of Paul's tent-making
questions.D: ignoring Paul's command to earn one's own living
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 3:10-12: 'If any one will not work, let him not eat.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus himself was known in Nazareth as 'the carpenter, the son of Mary', and Paul was a tent-maker. These facts teach that
questions.A: only carpenters and tent-makers can serve God
questions.B: manual labour is honourable and compatible with spiritual calling
questions.C: religious leaders should never engage in manual work
questions.D: trade is a hindrance to the preaching of the gospel
questions.explanation: Mark 6:3 and Acts 18:3: the Lord and the apostle both dignified ordinary work.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Thessalonians that at the coming of the Lord 'the dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are alive... shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air'. He wrote this to
questions.A: reveal the exact date of the second coming
questions.B: warn the Thessalonians to stop working and wait for the Lord
questions.C: comfort believers who grieved that their dead would miss the Lord's coming
questions.D: prove that only the living would be saved
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18: 'Therefore comfort one another with these words.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the Father only.' A preacher who announces the exact date of Christ's return is
questions.A: interpreting the signs of the times correctly
questions.B: fulfilling the duty to watch and be ready
questions.C: following the example of Paul in Thessalonica
questions.D: claiming knowledge that Jesus said belongs to the Father alone
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:36; Acts 1:7: 'It is not for you to know times or seasons.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter wrote that scoffers would say, 'Where is the promise of his coming?' and answered that 'the Lord is not slow about his promise... but is forbearing toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance'. The apparent delay of the second coming is therefore due to
questions.A: God's forgetfulness of the promise He made
questions.B: God's patience in giving people opportunity to repent
questions.C: the church's failure to pray for Christ's return
questions.D: the opposition of the Roman emperor
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:3-9: 'with the Lord one day is as a thousand years'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church member sells his property, stops working and sits waiting for the Lord's return. Paul's letters to the Thessalonians show that his conduct is
questions.A: the pattern the apostles followed after the ascension
questions.B: commendable, because it shows total faith in the promise
questions.C: mistaken, because believers are to keep working quietly while they wait
questions.D: required of every Christian who expects the Lord's return
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 3:6-12: idleness in the name of the second coming was rebuked.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the talents the master returned 'after a long time' and settled accounts with his servants. Applied to the second coming, the parable teaches that believers should
questions.A: use faithfully what God has entrusted to them until the Lord returns
questions.B: bury their gifts safely so that nothing is lost
questions.C: expect the master to return within a few days
questions.D: trade with the master's money for their own profit
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:14-30: 'Well done, good and faithful servant... enter into the joy of your master.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said the coming of the Son of man would be 'as were the days of Noah... they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came'. The point is that
questions.A: his coming will be sudden and will surprise those who are unprepared
questions.B: eating, drinking and marriage are sinful activities
questions.C: the world will end by a second flood
questions.D: only eight people will be saved at the second coming
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:37-42: 'Watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James wrote, 'If you show partiality, you commit sin, and are convicted by the law as transgressors.' He described partiality as a breach of
questions.A: the royal law, 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself'
questions.B: the law of the Sabbath, 'Six days you shall labour'
questions.C: the law of tithing, 'Bring the full tithes into the storehouse'
questions.D: the law of circumcision given to Abraham and his seed
questions.explanation: James 2:8-9: favouritism denies the equal love the law commands.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James asked, 'Has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom?... But you have dishonoured the poor man.' He pointed out the folly of favouring the rich, who
questions.A: oppressed the believers, dragged them into court and blasphemed the name
questions.B: had built the synagogue in which the believers met
questions.C: were more likely to become Christians than the poor
questions.D: had been chosen by God to lead the church
questions.explanation: James 2:5-7: the church was flattering the very class that persecuted it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A pastor gives the children of wealthy members leading roles in every programme while ignoring the poor children. This is the sin James called
questions.A: partiality or respect of persons
questions.B: the works of the flesh
questions.C: grieving the Holy Spirit
questions.D: quenching the Spirit
questions.explanation: James 2:1: 'show no partiality as you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter said at the house of Cornelius, 'Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality, but in every nation any one who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.' This truth means that in the church
questions.A: no race or nation may be treated as second-class
questions.B: all members must adopt Jewish customs
questions.C: Gentiles should form separate congregations
questions.D: only Romans may hold positions of leadership
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34-35: God's impartiality is the basis for the church's unity across nations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul warned Timothy, 'In the presence of God and of Christ Jesus and of the elect angels I charge you to keep these rules without favour, doing nothing from partiality.' This shows that impartiality is required especially in
questions.A: church discipline and the treatment of elders
questions.B: the choice of hymns for worship
questions.C: the payment of the temple tax
questions.D: the interpretation of prophecy
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 5:19-21: charges against elders were to be handled fairly, without prejudice or favour.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James wrote, 'You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it on your passions.' A student who prays for wealth so that he can outshine his friends is
questions.A: asking wrongly, with selfish motives
questions.B: praying according to the will of God
questions.C: exercising the prayer of faith that James commended
questions.D: praying like Elijah for rain
questions.explanation: James 4:3: motive matters in prayer; God does not supply selfish desires.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In Gethsemane Jesus prayed, 'My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt.' This teaches that effective prayer
questions.A: expresses honest desire yet submits to the Father's will
questions.B: always obtains exactly what is requested
questions.C: should never mention the suffering one wants to avoid
questions.D: must be repeated three times to be heard
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:39-44: Jesus' submission is the model of prayer 'according to his will' (1 John 5:14).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'Whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you receive it, and you will. And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against any one.' Two conditions for effective prayer given here are
questions.A: faith and a forgiving spirit
questions.B: fasting and loud crying
questions.C: long prayers and many words
questions.D: standing and facing Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Mark 11:24-25: believing prayer and forgiveness of others go together.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told a parable of a friend who came at midnight asking for three loaves, and said that 'because of his importunity he will rise and give him whatever he needs'. The lesson is that
questions.A: persistence in prayer is rewarded
questions.B: neighbours should not be disturbed at night
questions.C: God is reluctant and must be worn down
questions.D: prayer should be made only at midnight
questions.explanation: Luke 11:5-10: 'Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus warned, 'In praying do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their many words.' A prayer leader who believes God answers only long, shouted prayers has forgotten that
questions.A: the Father knows what we need before we ask him
questions.B: God hears only prayers offered in the temple
questions.C: prayer must be made in a language no one understands
questions.D: long prayers are always a sign of great faith
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:7-8: prayer is addressed to a loving Father, not to a deity who must be impressed by volume.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James taught, 'Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will save the sick man.' He added, 'Confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another,' because
questions.A: unconfessed sin can hinder prayer and healing within the fellowship
questions.B: the elders cannot pray unless they know every sin of the member
questions.C: confession replaces the need for medical treatment
questions.D: only public sinners fall ill
questions.explanation: James 5:14-16: 'The prayer of a righteous man has great power in its effects.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse them. Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep... Repay no one evil for evil.' A Christian whose neighbour damaged her fence and who then pours refuse into his compound has violated
questions.A: the command to repay no one evil for evil
questions.B: the command to rejoice with those who rejoice
questions.C: the command to be subject to the governing authorities
questions.D: the command to owe no one anything
questions.explanation: Romans 12:14-21: 'Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul urged, 'If possible, so far as it depends upon you, live peaceably with all.' The phrase 'so far as it depends upon you' recognises that
questions.A: a Christian should do his own part for peace even though others may refuse it
questions.B: peace is impossible and need not be attempted
questions.C: Christians should withdraw from all contact with unbelievers
questions.D: peace should be pursued only with fellow believers
questions.explanation: Romans 12:18: the believer is responsible for his own conduct, not for the response of others.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter wrote, 'Maintain good conduct among the Gentiles, so that in case they speak against you as wrongdoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God.' This teaches that a Christian's behaviour in the community
questions.A: is a witness that can silence slander and bring glory to God
questions.B: should be hidden from unbelievers to avoid persecution
questions.C: does not matter as long as his faith is sincere
questions.D: should copy the standards of the surrounding society
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:12, 15: 'by doing right you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.' A Christian trader known throughout the market for honest scales and fair prices is
questions.A: letting her light shine so that others may glorify God
questions.B: seeking the praise of men rather than of God
questions.C: hiding her lamp under a bushel
questions.D: practising her piety before men to be seen by them
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:16: visible good works that point to the Father are the intended witness of disciples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Romans, 'Owe no one anything, except to love each other; for he who loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law.' A Christian who refuses to repay a loan to an unbeliever, saying the man is 'a sinner anyway', is
questions.A: ignoring Paul's teaching on honesty and love towards all
questions.B: obeying the command to have no fellowship with darkness
questions.C: correctly applying the principle of grace over law
questions.D: practising the communal sharing of the early church
questions.explanation: Romans 13:8-10: love does no wrong to a neighbour, and debts must be honoured.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for edifying, as fits the occasion, that it may impart grace to those who hear.' A church member who spreads gossip about a neighbour's marriage is
questions.A: using speech to tear down rather than to build up
questions.B: exercising the gift of discernment
questions.C: speaking the truth in love
questions.D: correcting a fellow believer as Paul commanded
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:29-31: slander and evil talk grieve the Holy Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Simon the sorcerer offered money for the power to confer the Holy Spirit, Peter said, 'Your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!' A candidate who pays a bribe to be ordained a church minister is repeating
questions.A: the sin of Simon, treating the things of God as items for sale
questions.B: the generosity of Barnabas, who sold a field
questions.C: the faith of Cornelius, who gave alms liberally
questions.D: the zeal of Apollos, who was mighty in the scriptures
questions.explanation: Acts 8:18-24: the attempt to buy spiritual office or power is called 'simony' after him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Judas Iscariot agreed to betray Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver. John notes that Judas 'was a thief, and as he had the money box he used to take what was put into it'. This suggests that
questions.A: small acts of dishonesty prepared the way for his great betrayal
questions.B: Judas was forced by the priests to betray Jesus
questions.C: the other disciples also stole from the money box
questions.D: Judas gave all the money to the poor
questions.explanation: John 12:6 and Matthew 26:14-16: corruption in small matters grew into treachery.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: John the Baptist told the tax collectors, 'Collect no more than is appointed you,' and the soldiers, 'Rob no one by violence or by false accusation, and be content with your wages.' A customs officer who demands 'settlement' above the official duty is
questions.A: committing the abuse that John condemned
questions.B: following the advice given to the soldiers
questions.C: showing the fruit that befits repentance
questions.D: obeying the command to render to Caesar
questions.explanation: Luke 3:12-14: John required repentance to show itself in honest handling of public office.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Zacchaeus said, 'Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have defrauded any one of anything, I restore it fourfold.' A converted contractor who returns money he had inflated on government projects is showing
questions.A: the restitution that accompanies genuine repentance
questions.B: that salvation can be bought with money
questions.C: the tithe required by the law of Moses
questions.D: the communal sharing of the early church
questions.explanation: Luke 19:8-9: Jesus responded, 'Today salvation has come to this house.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'The love of money is the root of all evils; it is through this craving that some have wandered away from the faith and pierced their hearts with many pangs.' Note that Paul condemns
questions.A: the love of money, not money itself
questions.B: all possession of money by Christians
questions.C: the use of money for trade and business
questions.D: the payment of wages to church workers
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:10: it is the craving for riches, not wealth as such, that leads to ruin.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The law of Moses commanded, 'You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds the officials, and subverts the cause of those who are in the right.' The bribe is condemned because it
questions.A: perverts justice against the innocent
questions.B: reduces the income of the government
questions.C: is a form of gift that only the rich can afford
questions.D: was permitted for judges but not for kings
questions.explanation: Exodus 23:8 and Deuteronomy 16:19: bribery corrupts judgment and oppresses the righteous.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Corinthians, 'Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God? You are not your own; you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.' He used this argument to
questions.A: urge believers to flee from sexual immorality
questions.B: encourage them to build a temple in Corinth
questions.C: explain why Christians should fast regularly
questions.D: justify the payment of the temple tax
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:18-20: immorality sins against one's own body, which belongs to God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Joseph resisted Potiphar's wife although she pressed him 'day after day', and when she caught his garment he fled out of the house. His example teaches that
questions.A: avoiding the occasion of temptation is wiser than trusting one's own strength
questions.B: servants should always obey their masters' wives
questions.C: a false accusation can be avoided by staying near the tempter
questions.D: faithfulness is guaranteed to bring immediate reward
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:7-12: Joseph refused, avoided her, and finally fled, though it cost him prison.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student says, 'My body is mine; what I do with it in private is nobody's business.' Paul's answer would be that
questions.A: the believer's body belongs to the Lord, having been bought with a price
questions.B: private sins are not counted as sins by God, so the matter is closed
questions.C: the body is evil and therefore what is done with it does not matter
questions.D: only public immorality brings judgment, while private sins are overlooked
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:13, 19-20: 'The body is not meant for immorality, but for the Lord.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul instructed that a man in the Corinthian church who was living with his father's wife should be removed from the fellowship, because
questions.A: a little leaven leavens the whole lump, and open immorality tolerated corrupts the whole church
questions.B: the man had refused to pay his tithe to the church for more than a year despite repeated warnings
questions.C: the church had no authority to forgive any sin and could only hand offenders over to the state
questions.D: his father had complained to the Roman governor, who threatened to close the church in Corinth
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:1-13: discipline aimed at the offender's restoration and the purity of the church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The writer of Hebrews said, 'Let marriage be held in honour among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled; for God will judge the immoral and adulterous.' This teaches that
questions.A: sexual relations belong within marriage, which God honours and protects
questions.B: marriage is a lower state than remaining single
questions.C: adultery is judged only by human courts
questions.D: married people are exempt from sexual temptation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:4: marriage is honourable and its exclusive bond is guarded by God's judgment.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nathan told David, 'You have despised the word of the LORD... the sword shall never depart from your house.' This shows that David's adultery
questions.A: was forgiven but still brought lasting consequences on his family
questions.B: was overlooked because he was king
questions.C: had no effect on anyone except Bathsheba
questions.D: was punished by his immediate removal from the throne
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:9-14: 'The LORD has put away your sin', yet the child died and strife followed in David's house.
